program: Fort Bend and Waller integrated clinical access
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: AccessHealth provides primary, dental, behavioral and other healthcare services to low-income families in Fort Bend and Waller counties.
Its integrated clinics also offer pharmacy, nutrition, HIV and hepatitis care, with insurance acceptance and income-based fees.
The organization connects patients with continuing treatment and assistance rather than relying only on episodic medical visits.
strengths: Current primary services identify insurance, sliding fees and medication-access mechanisms.
Three original annual returns verify recipient identity and current recognized cost.
Original service counts distinguish encounters and nutrition recipients rather than claiming all contacts are unique treatment completions.
reservations: Repeated visits, household duplication and clinical treatment completion are not verified.
The modeled adult utility and actual net household resource effects are unsupported priors.
Whole-recipient cost includes additional services and geography beyond this narrow adult medical channel.

sections.what: AccessHealth provides primary, dental, behavioral and other healthcare services to low-income families in Fort Bend and Waller counties. Its integrated clinics also offer pharmacy, nutrition, HIV and hepatitis care, with insurance acceptance and income-based fees. The organization connects patients with continuing treatment and assistance rather than relying only on episodic medical visits.
sections.monitoring: FY2025 original reports 51,493 medical encounters, 6,670 dental encounters, 8,146 behavioral encounters and additional nutrition/optometry contacts. These are not unique patients and are not added into one cohort. WIC recipients across five counties are not extra independent Houston clinical or cash beneficiaries. Request medical visit-to-unique-adult and household ratios, completed dose, clinical utility follow-up, actual household net payments and alternative-care use. Current Medicaid/Medicare/private insurance, sliding fees and 340B arrangements form the reimbursement counterfactual.
sections.qualitative: Current primary services identify insurance, sliding fees and medication-access mechanisms. Three original annual returns verify recipient identity and current recognized cost. Original service counts distinguish encounters and nutrition recipients rather than claiming all contacts are unique treatment completions. Repeated visits, household duplication and clinical treatment completion are not verified. The modeled adult utility and actual net household resource effects are unsupported priors. Whole-recipient cost includes additional services and geography beyond this narrow adult medical channel. Original EIN 74-1951476 matches the AccessHealth recipient. Fort Bend and Waller clinical target is within the Houston MSA; service locations do not prove all patients reside there. Recipient-owned giving route is checked, not a transaction, funding restriction or donation-sensitive expansion.
sections.cost: The conditional limited-channel annual reference is $125.74 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 2.913491 clinical QALYs plus -0.365733 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000795 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not verified next-gift response. Full recognized annual current expense is $32,035,425. Observed 51,493 encounters × judged .15 adult household opportunities per encounter × .2 additional annual response gives 1,544.79 exposed household proxies. The .15 mapping explicitly combines .25 distinct medical episodes per encounter with .6 adult-household share, neither observed. The clinical subset of 308.958 adults receives judged .02 utility for .5 finite years; this is not a trial-calibrated effect or visit-to-health conversion. Independent resource success .2 with hypothetical $200 actual otherwise-paid care expense avoided after alternative provider, taxes and benefits uses positive overlap .5 minus full $30 one-off copay, travel, childcare or foregone-pay burden. Success households net $70 and other exposed households lose full $30. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption is modeled with a single joint log. Retail 340B medicine value, gross wages and ordinary survivor earnings are excluded. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens; positive-only overlap preserves full negative resources and union harms. ResourceYears means fraction of one year's gains, not repeated lifetime savings. Partner/payer opportunity costs are distinct from participant burdens; central external zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Whole expense versus narrow adult medical numerator leaves other portfolio benefits, burdens and marginal financing unknown.
sections.funding: Current fiscal year ends June 30, 2025. Original recognized current expenses are FY2025 $32,035,425, FY2024 $30,581,547 and FY2023 $27,842,283. FY2025 Schedule D audited expense $32,061,430 less $26,005 PRIOR YEAR ADJUSTMENT reconciles to $32,035,425; this is not an omitted donated-service expense or new current service cost. No populated netted event/rental/inventory or excluded donated-service fields were recovered; unrecognized volunteer/partner resources remain unknown, not factual zero. Reimbursements, public grants, 340B and WIC funding are baseline mechanisms; donations are not assumed to create all existing services.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Narrow Fort Bend/Waller adult medical channel inside Houston MSA; .95 local share is judgment, not inferred from five-county WIC coverage.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Insurance, Medicaid/Medicare, other FQHC and public/charity treatment, sliding fees, 340B access and partner funding remain baseline; only incremental annual care and net household resources count.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Medical encounters mapped by explicit weak priors to unique adult household opportunities; additional appropriate treatment and finite symptom relief, not visits as QALYs.
